reasoning: Montana is currently best characterized as **R+19 to R+20** in the 2026 U.S. Senate race based on the most recent statewide polling from late July and early August, with Republican Kurt Alme leading either in a three-way field or in the aggregated polling average. I did not find any recent Montana presidential general-election polling for this cycle, so the Senate race is the only current-race margin I can report from the last 45 days.

sources.name: Tavern Research via PollsMax
sources.details: A Montana Senate poll found Kurt Alme at 49%, Seth Bodnar at 25%, and Alani Bankhead at 24%, implying an Alme lead of 24 points in the full field.

sources.name: GQR via PollsMax
sources.details: A GQR poll of Montana likely voters showed Alme ahead 41% to 27% in the race summary displayed by the polling average page, a 14-point lead.

sources.name: Independent Center Voice & Independent Leadership Council
sources.details: A statewide survey of 793 likely Montana voters found Alme leading with 36%, followed by Bodnar at 24% and Bankhead at 22%, a 14-point lead over the nearest Democrat.

sources.name: Strength In Numbers
sources.details: A poll shared by Strength In Numbers found Alme at 41% in the current four-way race, with Bodnar at 25%, Bankhead at 24%, and Austin at 2%, indicating a 16-point lead over the closest challenger.

sources.name: PollsMax polling average
sources.details: Polling average page shows Alme at 44.1% and the nearest opponent at 25.1%, for an average Republican lead of 19.0 points.
